metaDescription: SecuEdge protects construction firms, contractors and engineering companies from ransomware targeting BIM files and project data, subcontractor network abuse and vulnerable VPN appliances.

hero.headline: Protect Every Blueprint, Every Project, Every Site
hero.sub: Bouygues Construction had 1,000+ TB of project data locked. Bird Construction faced a $9M CAD ransom demand. Ransomware attacks on construction doubled from 2023 to 2024 — and construction is now a top-three most attacked sector.

stats.label: Bouygues Construction data locked by Maze ransomware
Construction industry's rank among most attacked sectors

challenges.title: Ransomware Targeting Irreplaceable BIM Files
challenges.desc: Building Information Modelling files and project specifications represent years of engineering work. Losing them is not just a data loss — it can halt active construction sites and trigger contract penalties.

challenges.title: Unmanaged Subcontractor Network Access
challenges.desc: Dozens of subcontractors, site managers and engineers connect to project networks using personal devices with no MDM, no security baseline and no visibility — each one a potential entry point.

challenges.title: Vulnerable Third-Party VPN Appliances
challenges.desc: Akira ransomware specifically targeted SonicWall SSL VPN appliances (CVE-2024-40766) widely used by construction firms for remote site access. Arctic Wolf documented a surge of construction victims through this exact vector.

challenges.title: No Segmentation Between Office and Jobsite
challenges.desc: A compromised laptop on a jobsite WiFi network typically has a routed path to the corporate file server — one infected device from a sub becomes access to the entire project archive.

challenges.title: BEC and Wire Fraud on Accounts Payable
challenges.desc: Construction firms routinely move large sums between principals, contractors and subcontractors. Impersonation of finance contacts via email compromise is a highly lucrative attack given the transaction sizes involved.

challenges.title: Remote Site Management Systems Exposed
challenges.desc: Project management portals, SCADA-adjacent building automation systems and remote monitoring tools are often left internet-facing without VPN protection — reachable from anywhere in the world.

threats.title: Mass Project Data Encryption
threats.desc: Maze ransomware required unrestricted SMB access to network shares to encrypt them. Bouygues had 237 computers locked and 200 GB stolen; Bird Construction lost 60 GB of federal project contracts and subcontractor details.

threats.title: VPN Appliance Exploitation
threats.desc: Akira ransomware's dedicated construction campaign exploited SonicWall SSL VPN CVE-2024-40766. Firms that had deployed SonicWall for remote site access found their own VPN was the entry point.

threats.title: Subcontractor Device Propagation
threats.desc: A subcontractor device with pre-existing malware connects to the site WiFi. Without segmentation, that device has the same network path to project servers as the project manager's workstation.

threats.title: Pre-Ransomware SMB Reconnaissance
threats.desc: Ransomware actors spend days mapping internal file shares via SMB enumeration before encrypting. This reconnaissance phase is detectable — but only with network monitoring in place.

approach.title: Replace Vulnerable VPN Appliances
approach.desc: SecuEdge's OpenVPN and IPSec replace SonicWall, Cisco and Citrix VPN appliances — eliminating the CVE-2024-40766 attack surface entirely. Remote site access is authenticated via hardened SecuEdge tunnels with certificate and MFA.

approach.title: Isolate Subcontractors via Captive Portal
approach.desc: Subcontractors get internet access via captive-portal-authenticated WiFi in a dedicated VLAN with no route to project file servers. Site visitors and personal devices are completely isolated from project data.

approach.title: Segment Office, Jobsite and BIM Servers
approach.desc: Project file servers, office workstations and jobsite networks sit in separate firewall zones. SMB access from the site VLAN to the BIM server VLAN requires an explicit firewall allow rule — Maze-style propagation stops at the first boundary.

approach.title: Detect Pre-Ransomware Reconnaissance
approach.desc: SecuEdge's network monitoring logs SMB enumeration and unusual internal scanning patterns — the pre-encryption reconnaissance phase that ransomware actors conduct. Catching this phase prevents the encryption event entirely.

capabilities.title: VPN (OpenVPN + IPSec) — Replaces Legacy Appliances
capabilities.desc: Harden remote site access with SecuEdge VPN — replacing vulnerable SonicWall, Fortinet and Cisco appliances with a single authenticated, monitored gateway for all remote project access.

capabilities.title: Captive Portal for Subcontractor WiFi
capabilities.desc: Authenticate every subcontractor and site visitor at network entry. Their devices land in an isolated VLAN with internet access only — no route to project file shares, BIM servers or corporate systems.

capabilities.title: Firewall Segmentation (Office / Site / BIM)
capabilities.desc: Separate firewall zones for corporate office, project file and BIM servers, jobsite networks and subcontractor WiFi — with explicit allow rules governing which zone can speak to which.

capabilities.title: DNS & Content Category Blocking
capabilities.desc: Block known Maze, Akira and construction-sector ransomware C2 domains at the DNS layer — preventing encryption key exchange even after initial infection on a workstation.

capabilities.title: Network Monitoring & SMB Anomaly Detection
capabilities.desc: Detect pre-ransomware reconnaissance — unusual SMB enumeration, internal port scans and after-hours bulk file access — before the encryption event that causes the damage.

capabilities.title: Bandwidth Management & Exfil Detection
capabilities.desc: Alert on bulk outbound data transfers from project file servers — the data staging that precedes double-extortion ransomware demands.

process.title: Exposure & Network Assessment
process.desc: Identify all VPN appliances with known CVEs, map SMB-accessible file shares, audit subcontractor network access and locate internet-exposed management systems on jobsite networks.

process.title: Segment and Harden
process.desc: Deploy hardened VPN replacing legacy appliances, create BIM server and jobsite VLANs, configure captive portal for subcontractor WiFi and enable DNS blocking with SMB anomaly monitoring.

process.title: Ongoing Site Security
process.desc: Review subcontractor access as teams change across project phases, update DNS block lists, verify firewall rules when new systems are connected to site networks.

faqs.q: How does SecuEdge stop ransomware from encrypting our BIM and project files?
faqs.a: SecuEdge breaks the ransomware chain at two points. First, DNS blocking prevents C2 callbacks — without receiving encryption keys, ransomware cannot proceed. Second, firewall segmentation means a compromised workstation on the office network cannot reach BIM server VLANs without an explicit allow rule — lateral movement stops at the zone boundary.

faqs.q: Our subcontractors need to access project portals on site. How does SecuEdge handle that?
faqs.a: Subcontractors connect to a captive-portal-authenticated SSID that places their devices in an isolated VLAN with internet access only. For portal access to internal project systems, we configure VPN credentials scoped to the specific systems that subcontractor role requires — no broader network access.

faqs.q: We use SonicWall for remote site access. Is that a problem?
faqs.a: CVE-2024-40766 in SonicWall SSL VPN was the specific entry point Akira ransomware used in the documented surge against construction firms. SecuEdge can replace that appliance entirely — your remote site access runs through SecuEdge's hardened OpenVPN or IPSec gateway instead.

faqs.q: How quickly can SecuEdge be deployed across multiple active construction sites?
faqs.a: SecuEdge Frontier appliances are designed for rapid site deployment. Initial VPN hardening and VLAN segmentation for a project office takes hours. Captive portal configuration for a jobsite is a day's work. Sites can be brought online incrementally without disrupting active project operations.

cta.headline: Protect Your Projects From Blueprint to Completion
cta.sub: Replace vulnerable VPN appliances, isolate subcontractor networks and detect ransomware reconnaissance before a single file gets encrypted.
